  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 12, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR HUFF called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by members of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Rotary Club.

Members of the Palos Verdes Peninsula (PVP) Rotary Club introduced themselves,
including Julia Parton, PVP Rotary Club President, Greg O’Brien, Peartree Lane Oversight
Committee, Derald Sidler, PVP Rotary Foundation Chair, and Rick Humphrey, Community
Service Chair, and spoke about the history of the Rotary Club and explained its creation of
the Peartree Lane Relief Fund to facilitate donations and connect affected residents with
those who wish to help.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

  MONTH"

Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

A.  REQUEST TO ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2559, APPROVING AN INITIAL STUDY
  AND MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION (IS/MND), AND MITIGATION
  MONITORING AND REPORTING PROGRAM (MMRP) UNDER THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA) FOR A TRANSPORTATION
  ENHANCEMENT AND ADA IMPROVEMENT PROJECT AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH (PVDN) AND LONDON LN. (DAPPLEGRAY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL
  ENTRANCE); AND, TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR THE PROJECT WITH FUNDING BY A
  “MEASURE M FUNDING AGREEMENT MULTI-YEAR SUB REGIONAL PROGRAM”
  WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION
  AUTHORITY (LACMTA)

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the Public Hearing; 2) Take public
  testimony; 3) Discuss the issues; 4) Close the Public Hearing; 5) Adopt Resolution
  No. 2559 (Approving the project’s IS/MND and MMRP); and, 6) Direct staff to solicit
  bids for the project.

Public Works Director David Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from Connor Lynch, Suzette James, Lynn Yen, Sheri Allen,
Grant Mogford, and Aly Beck, all in opposition of the project as proposed, requesting further
evaluation, consideration, and discussion with community groups.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked the members of the community who came to voice
their opinions on this matter. He agreed that some aspects needed further consideration before
the project moves forwards, emphasizing concerns about the ability of emergency vehicles

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 12, 2023
 having thru-access during high-traffic school times near Dapplegray School. He asked Public
Works Director Wahba to discuss the Little League access road with the School District which
was brought up by a member of the public. He also asked staff to discuss staggered drop-off
and pick-up times with Dapplegray School. He explained the challenges with current State
legislation related to California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), Vehicle Miles Traveled
(VMT) and housing requirements.

Public Works Director Wahba explained similar projects that were done at various intersections
throughout the City. He also discussed the narrow Little League access road behind the school,
and the challenges and benefits of potentially widening it.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER expressed concern about cars passing on the right when
merger lanes are added at large intersections on Palos Verdes Drive North.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA echoed COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER’S concerns, and
supported the recommendation to continue the item for further discussion.

The City’s Traffic Engineer Joanne Itagaki noted that the length of the merger lanes would be
about 600 feet, and that the 1,000 feet in the plans includes the entire construction zone.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ echoed COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’S comments
regarding the challenges the City faces with current State legislation, and encouraged the
community to attend Traffic & Safety Committee meetings where the details of projects like this
are discussed.

It was the consensus of the City Council to continue this item for further discussion.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  DIRECT STAFF TO TABLE THE ISSUE AND BRING BACK TO THE CITY
  COUNCIL AFTER GETTING INPUT FROM THE FOLLOWING COMMUNITY
  GROUPS: PALOS VERDES PENINSULA SCHOOL BOARD, LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY SHERIFF AND FIRE DEPARTMENTS, THE PALOS VERDES
  PENINSULA PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE AND PARENTS OF DAPPLEGRAY
  ELEMENTARY STUDENTS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to enter into a Public Works
  Contract with Mariscal Painting Inc. (all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney), to
  repair the Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) equipment room attached
  to the south end of the City Hall building, and to make other necessary exterior wood
  repairs, including repainting the exterior of both the City Hall and Council Chambers
  buildings, in the bid amount of $162,000, plus a 10% contingency ($16,200), plus
  $1,000 for permit and inspection services provided by Willdan Engineering, for a
  grand total of $179,200.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public Works Director Wahba explained that the HVAC room and City Hall building are two
separate structures and slabs in response to MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ.

SEPTEMBER 12, 2023

No public testimony was received.

  VOTE:

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA attended the Clean Power Alliance board meeting.

MAYOR HUFF attended the Rancho Palos Verdes (RPV) City Council meeting to congratulate
them on their 50th anniversary and presented a certificate. MAYOR HUFF also attended the
RPV 50th Anniversary Gala.

MAYOR HUFF also announced the annual City Celebration on Saturday, September 23, 2023.

MAYOR HUFF also reported that many members of the City Council will be attending the Cal
Cities Annual Conference in Sacramento next week.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 12, 2023
 12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  OPPOSITION LETTER FOR ASSEMBLY BILL AB 825

  Recommendation: That the City Council discuss the issues and authorize the Mayor to
  sign the attached letter in opposition to AB 825.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material.)

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER stated that electric bike (e-bike) safety was discussed at a
recent Equestrian Committee meeting specifically safety concerns on the trails.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from Equestrian Committee members Vicki Shinn and Terry
Griggs as well as Charlene O’Neill, President of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Horseman’s
Association, all expressing concerns about e-bikes and the safety of riders and horses in the
City.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ noted that the City Council fights for local control, and moved to
authorize the Mayor to sign the letter in opposition of AB 825.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER suggested the e-bike issue be brought back to the
Equestrian Committee and for the Committee to make new recommendations to the City
Council.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA proposed another discussion of e-bikes on a future City
Council agenda.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:
